exposure: High output cardiac failure (suspected cause of hydrops)
outcome: Resolution of hydrops (implied by normal baby delivery)
Delivery of a normal female baby with good APGAR score
Presence of huge chorioangioma of placenta (at delivery)
cohort: A single 35-year-old pregnant woman (G3P1L1A1) who presented at 32 weeks gestation with preterm rupture of membranes and whose fetus developed non-immune hydrops.
finding: Chorioangiomas of the placenta should be considered in the differential diagnosis of non-immune hydrops, necessitating regular fetal surveillance and timely intervention to improve postnatal survival.
